check/ask: Ask a model nine times seven, and sample four answers: sixty three, sixty three, fifty four, sixty three.
check/check: No person has to judge them. A program compares each final answer with the known one: a reward, r, of one if they match and zero if not. One, one, zero, one.
check/code: Code is checked the same way: run each program on tests, and reward it if every test passes.
check/format: DeepSeek's R1, in 2025, trained like this, plus a small reward for the right format: its steps between think tags, then the answer.
check/judge: The other way is a learned judge, a second network trained to score answers. The model can learn to please it with answers that are still wrong. A checker cannot be fooled: only a right answer earns one.
group/mean: These four rewards are a GRPO group. Their mean is three of four, zero point seven five: the share that pass, the pass rate.
group/std: Their standard deviation is about zero point four three three.
group/right: Each right answer's advantage is one minus zero point seven five, over zero point four three three: zero point five eight.
group/wrong: The wrong one gets minus zero point seven five over zero point four three three: minus one point seven three, a large push down.
edge/all: Had all four been right, every reward would equal the mean, and every advantage would be zero. All wrong, the same. That prompt teaches nothing.
edge/edge: So the prompts worth training on sit at the edge of what the model can do: it solves them some of the time.
edge/long: Only the final answer is checked, never the steps. Yet over training, the answers grow longer: chains that check their own steps land on the right answer more often, so they get pushed up.
try/p1: Try one. Five answers to seventeen plus twenty five say forty two, forty two, thirty two, forty two, forty two. The rewards' standard deviation is zero point four. What is the advantage of answer two, counting from zero?
try/r: The checker gives one, one, zero, one, one.
try/mean: Four of five pass, so the mean is zero point eight.
try/a1: Answer two got zero. Zero minus zero point eight is minus zero point eight, and over zero point four that is minus two.
try/count: The mean also runs backwards: eight answers with a mean reward of zero point six two five means zero point six two five times eight, five, passed.
